content:
Recent Updates:

* Tie-Break System: Implemented a new scoring system to resolve draws. Players now earn tie-break points based on their aligned marbles (5 marbles = 500 pts, 4 = 100 pts, 3 = 10 pts, 2 = 1 pt).
* Endgame Cinematic Overhaul: Upgraded the endgame UI to display final player rankings (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th) instead of just "Winner/Draw". The winner's score is now highlighted in glowing gold.
* Statement Updates: The game rules (both English and French) have been updated across all leagues to clearly explain the new Tie-Break scoring conditions.

Leagues
* Are you able to specify league names, i.e. Wood/Bronze/etc. instead of Wood 4 to Wood 1, which seem to be the default? (Example: https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/game-of-life-or-death )

Note: The comments below apply to all leagues unless otherwise specified.

Introduction
* Please ensure that the league names are correct.

* (Level 2 only) Please change "Free-For-All" to "free-for-all".

* (Level 3 only) Please remove "physical".

Goal
* Consider removing the word "official".

Rules (Levels 3 and 4)
* Rotate: Please keep the terms "counter-clockwise" and "clockwise".

* Please remove "physical".

Game Input/Output
* Please provide the following as initialisation input:
  • Number of players
  • Player ID

* Please format "." using the <const> tag instead of the <code> tag.

* (Levels 3 and 4) Please specify:

  • "A single line containing 4 space-separated values" for Option A.

  • "A single line containing 5 space-separated values" for Option B.

* (Levels 3 and 4) Please restore the descriptions of x, y, block and dir.

Constraints
* Please include the time limits.

Stub
* Please change the comment "'0' is player 0, '1' is player 1." to "'0' to '3' indicates a marble placed by the player with that ID."

* Please ensure that the league name "Silver league" is correct (it may be "Wood 2" instead).

Referee
* The "No output provided" exception can be removed as it's never triggered even when the output is an empty string (I assume this is because the `outputs` list is never empty).

Viewer
* Consider displaying past actions without the word "Played" and using a larger font size.

* Consider adding tooltips that display coordinates.

Your initial questions
* Since I don't spend much time playing multiplayer games, I think it's better for other players to share their opinions.

Thanks.

Here is Pentago Arena Edition! It’s based on an existing game but adapted for the Arena. :D

I have a few questions:

- As it stands, is it enough to make it a multi-league game? :O
- Should I add an extra action for the Gold League? Or plan for a larger board?
- Or would it be better to make all actions available right from the Bronze League?
- Should I allow two players on a 9x9 board?

Etc. :D

Any suggestions or comments are welcome! 

Enjoy! :)

No, it seems I don't have access to the league names; I renamed them.
Points addressed and pushed! :) Thanks!

Thank you! The updates look good. I only have a few minor suggestions left:

Game Input/Output
* Consider moving `size` to the initialisation input, since it remains constant throughout the game.

* Next `size` lines:
  • If `size` is moved to the initialisation input, you can remove the word "Next".

  • Please apply the "statement-lineno" formatting.

* Optional: Consider removing the SWAP keyword from the output format for consistency, since option A doesn't require a corresponding ROTATE keyword.

Thanks again.

All done! Thanks for the high-quality review, as always! :)
Perhaps I should also remove the "swap" keyword from the league ribbon?

You're welcome! 🙂

> league ribbon
Are you referring to the Level 3 (Wood 2) league introduction? If so, I'd suggest changing <action>SWAP</action> to simply SWAP, for consistency with the league preview section.

* I don't see the GitHub referee source updated yet. I assume the version on CG is more up to date?

* I have one remaining minor suggestion, but there's no need to address it immediately. It can wait, especially since the player counts and board sizes for each league may still change based on feedback from other reviewers.

  In the Input section, when a value is fixed, consider stating it directly instead of giving a range to avoid confusion:

  • Number of players: state 2 in Level 1, and 3 or 4 in the higher levels.

  • Player ID: state 0 or 1 in Level 1, and 0 to 3 in the higher levels.

  • Board size: state 6 in Level 1, and 9 in the higher levels.

Tie-break Score
* The current description leaves some aspects unspecified. Consider rewriting it as follows:

##########
If the board is full, or if multiple players form a line of 5 simultaneously, the winner is determined by a tie-break score.

For each player, consider every maximal contiguous line of their marbles in the four directions (horizontal, vertical, and the two diagonals). Each line contributes:

* Length 5 or more: 500 points
* Length 4: 100 points
* Length 3: 10 points
* Length 2: 1 point
* Length 1: 0 points

The player with the highest total score wins. If multiple players have the same highest tie-break score, the game ends in a draw between those players.
##########

Note 1: Please format the numbers using the <const> tag.

Note 2: It's theoretically possible for multiple players to simultaneously form a line longer than 5. For an example, see this replay: https://www.codingame.com/replay/896676961

Initialization Input
* (Mainly for Levels 2 to 4, though you may apply this to Level 1 as well.) Line 2: Please change 3 to "<var>playerCount</var> - 1".

Viewer
* Consider highlighting "1st" in glowing gold as well, to match the score.

Referee
* The referee contains new code for the "pie rule" in 2-player games, but this rule is never mentioned in the statement. My inclination would be to remove it, since it only applies to one league and is no longer relevant once players progress to the later leagues.

Thanks.
Thanks for this new revision! The changes have been made! :)

The update looks good. Thanks.

One point about the console. It currently displays two values: the final score and the tie-break score. The final score isn't described anywhere in the statement, while the tie-break score appears to determine the ranking of the non-winning players.

Would it be possible to display only a single score in the console?

One option would be to define the 1000000 score explicitly in the statement. For example, a player who is the sole player to form a line of 5 would receive a score of 1000000.

The other option would be to keep the 1000000 value internal and use a separate win flag in the code instead.

In either case, the scoring rules should naturally belong in the Rules section rather than under Victory Conditions. All non-eliminated players (including the cases where no player or multiple players form a line of 5) would receive the score currently referred to as the tie-break score.

What do you think?

Thanks! I went with your suggestion and unified everything into a single scoring system:

* A line of 5 now explicitly grants 10,000 points, guaranteeing a win over any other combinations.
* The artificial 1,000,000 points bonus has been completely removed from the Referee code.
* A single, clean score is now displayed in the console for all players.
* The detailed scoring explanation has been moved to the Rules section in the statement. The Victory Condition now simply states: "Have the highest score at the end of the game."

Everything has been updated and pushed to the repo. Thanks again for your help! :)

The revised scoring rule is much simpler and cleaner. Good job.

* Consider this replay: https://www.codingame.com/replay/896803221 . The scoring is correct. In the final frame, both lines of 6 (one belonging to the winner and one belonging to another player) are highlighted. What do you think? (I don't have any opinion.)

* One minor point about the stub. The final comment includes an example for X Y BLOCK DIR, but not for X Y B1 B2. Consider removing the example for consistency, although it's also perfectly fine to leave it as is.

Thanks! :)
Regarding the highlighted lines: I think it's actually fine as is. Since both players scored the massive 10K points bonus for forming a line of 5+, highlighting both lines visually explains to the viewers why the scores are so high and why it came down to a tie-break using the remaining shorter lines. It makes the endgame much easier to understand at a glance. 

For the stub: Great catch, I removed the example to keep the format consistent. The repo has been updated.

Your explanation makes sense.

I don't have any further comments for now 🙂
